title: CORNER Legal Templates Spec
summary: What AOM's client legal documents need to cover. NDA template, Master Service Agreement, and Acceptable Use Policy specs. Not legal advice. The strategic framework for a lawyer to draft from. Covers data isolation, AI liability, SLA commitments, and termination.
content:
CORNER Legal Templates Spec

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 For: Patrik (review), future legal counsel (drafting) Status: Strategic spec. NOT legal documents. These specs tell a lawyer exactly what AOM needs covered. The lawyer turns them into enforceable agreements. Depends on: Cyber insurance (Patrik, pending). Get the insurance first. The policy informs what the agreements need to disclaim.

Why This Matters Now

AOM is pre-revenue on Corner. The first client could sign within weeks. Before that happens, three documents need to exist:

  1. Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) -- signed before the audit starts. Protects both sides.
  2. Master Service Agreement (MSA) -- signed before the build starts. Covers ongoing relationship.
  3. Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) -- referenced in the MSA. What clients can and can't do with Corner.

Without these, AOM carries uncapped liability, no data protection commitments, and no clear terms for what happens when things go wrong. One bad client interaction without paperwork and the business is exposed.

Document 1: Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)

When it's signed

Before the audit ($2,500 engagement). Both parties sign. This protects AOM's proprietary system details and protects the client's business information shared during the audit.

What it needs to cover

Mutual confidentiality. Both AOM and the client agree not to share each other's confidential information. This is mutual, not one-sided. Clients share financials, operations, passwords. AOM shares its system architecture, agent configurations, and pricing strategies.

Definition of confidential information. Be specific:

  • Client side: business operations, financials, customer lists, trade secrets, passwords, API keys, internal communications
  • AOM side: Corner architecture, agent configurations, skills code, pricing models, client lists, internal processes, AI prompts and system instructions

Exclusions. Standard carve-outs:

  • Information that's already public
  • Information received from a third party without obligation
  • Information independently developed
  • Information required to be disclosed by law (with notice to the other party)

Duration. 3 years from date of disclosure. Industry standard for B2B tech NDAs.

Return/destruction. When the relationship ends, each party returns or destroys the other's confidential information within 30 days. Written confirmation required.

No reverse engineering. The client cannot attempt to replicate, reverse-engineer, or decompile Corner's system, agents, skills, or architecture. This is critical. AOM's system IS the product.

Injunctive relief. Both parties acknowledge that breach of confidentiality causes irreparable harm and either party may seek injunctive relief without proving damages. Standard but important.

Governing law. Arizona. All disputes resolved in Maricopa County courts.

Document 2: Master Service Agreement (MSA)

When it's signed

Before the system build begins (after the audit, when the client commits to a paid plan). This is the core business relationship document.

What it needs to cover

Section 1: Services Description

What AOM provides:

  • AI operations platform (Corner) hosted and managed by AOM
  • Configuration and deployment of AI agents tailored to client's business
  • Ongoing management, monitoring, and optimization
  • Regular updates and new feature releases
  • Support (response time commitments per tier)

What AOM does NOT provide:

  • Legal, financial, or regulatory advice through the AI system
  • Guarantee that AI output is 100% accurate (AI can make mistakes, like any tool or employee)
  • Replacement for professional services (CPA, attorney, licensed contractor work)
  • Client-side hardware, internet connectivity, or employee training beyond the onboarding period

Section 2: Data Handling and Privacy

Data isolation. Each client's data runs in a completely isolated environment (Docker container). No client can access another client's data. AOM personnel access client data only for support and maintenance purposes with client's implicit consent by signing the MSA.

Data ownership. The client owns their data. Period. AOM has a license to use the data solely for operating the Corner platform on the client's behalf. When the relationship ends, AOM exports the client's data and deletes it from AOM's systems within 30 days.

Data location. All client data stored on servers within the United States. Specify the hosting provider (Hetzner US or equivalent). If this changes, client is notified 30 days in advance.

AI model data. Client data is NOT used to train AI models. Client data does NOT leave the client's isolated environment except for API calls to the AI provider (Anthropic/OpenAI) which have their own enterprise data handling commitments (no training on API data). Reference the AI provider's enterprise terms.

Backup and recovery. Daily encrypted backups. 30-day retention. Recovery time objective: 4 hours. Recovery point objective: 24 hours (last daily backup). These numbers should be validated against actual infrastructure before going in the agreement.

Breach notification. If AOM discovers a data breach affecting the client's information, AOM notifies the client within 72 hours with: what happened, what data was affected, what AOM is doing about it, and what the client should do.

Section 3: Service Levels (SLA)

Uptime commitment: 99.5% monthly uptime (allows ~3.6 hours of downtime per month). Measured by external monitoring. Excludes scheduled maintenance (notified 48 hours in advance).

Response times by tier:

Priority Starter Growth Scale Enterprise
Critical (system down) 4 hours 2 hours 1 hour 30 minutes
High (feature broken) 8 hours 4 hours 2 hours 1 hour
Normal (question/request) 24 hours 12 hours 8 hours 4 hours

SLA credits. If uptime falls below 99.5% in a calendar month:

  • 99.0-99.4%: 10% credit on next month
  • 95.0-98.9%: 25% credit on next month
  • Below 95.0%: 50% credit on next month

Credits are the sole remedy for SLA failures. Total credits capped at 50% of one month's fees.

Section 4: AI-Specific Liability

This is the section that matters most. AI makes mistakes. The agreement needs to handle that clearly.

AOM's commitment: Best-effort AI operations. AOM configures, monitors, and optimizes the AI system using reasonable care and current best practices. AOM runs QA processes on agent output.

AOM's limitation: AI agents may produce incorrect, incomplete, or inappropriate output. The client is responsible for reviewing AI output before acting on it for: financial decisions, legal matters, client communications, safety-critical operations, and regulatory compliance.

Approval gates. Corner includes approval gates where the client reviews and approves certain outputs before they're sent or acted on. The client agrees to use these gates for sensitive operations. If the client disables approval gates and an error occurs, AOM's liability is limited.

No consequential damages. Standard limitation: AOM is not liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages. This includes lost revenue, lost data (beyond reasonable backup/recovery), lost business opportunities, or reputational harm caused by AI output.

Liability cap. Total liability capped at the fees paid by the client in the 12 months preceding the claim. Standard B2B SaaS cap.

Indemnification. Each party indemnifies the other against third-party claims arising from their own negligence or breach. AOM indemnifies client against claims that Corner infringes third-party IP rights. Client indemnifies AOM against claims arising from client's use of Corner output (e.g., client sends an AI-drafted email that defames someone).

Section 5: Intellectual Property

AOM owns Corner. The platform, the code, the agent architecture, the skills system, the design, the brand. All AOM's.

Client owns their data and their configurations. The specific agent names, business rules, workflow configurations, and operational data belong to the client.

Skills and customizations. If AOM builds custom skills or agents for a client, AOM owns the underlying code and methodology. The client has a license to use them as part of their Corner subscription. AOM can reuse the methodology (not the client's specific data) for other clients. If the client wants exclusive ownership of a custom skill, that's a separate negotiation with additional cost.

Section 6: Payment Terms

Billing cycle. Monthly, in advance. Due on the 1st. Auto-charged to card on file.

Late payment. 10 calendar days grace period. After 10 days: AOM may suspend service (not delete data). After 30 days: AOM may terminate. Client data retained for 60 days after termination, then deleted.

Price changes. 60 days written notice for any price increase. Current-term pricing honored through the end of the current billing period after notice.

No refunds for partial months. If client cancels mid-month, service continues through end of billing period.

Section 7: Termination

Client can terminate with 30 days written notice. No penalty. No early termination fee.

AOM can terminate with 30 days written notice for convenience, or immediately for: non-payment (after grace period), material breach, illegal use, abusive behavior toward AOM staff.

On termination:

  1. AOM exports client's data in standard format (JSON/CSV) within 15 business days
  2. Client's Corner instance is deactivated
  3. Client data deleted from AOM systems within 30 days of data export completion
  4. Any prepaid fees for unused service period are refunded pro-rata
  5. NDA survives termination (3-year duration continues)

Section 8: Miscellaneous

Force majeure. Standard clause. Neither party liable for delays caused by events beyond reasonable control (natural disasters, pandemics, AI provider outages, government actions).

Assignment. Neither party can assign the agreement without the other's consent, except in connection with a merger or acquisition (with notice).

Entire agreement. This MSA, plus the NDA and AUP, constitute the entire agreement. No side deals, verbal promises, or email commitments override these documents.

Amendments. Must be in writing, signed by both parties.

Governing law. Arizona. Maricopa County.

Dispute resolution. Good faith negotiation first (30 days). Then mediation (60 days). Then litigation. No mandatory arbitration (small business clients distrust it, and AOM wants flexibility).

Document 3: Acceptable Use Policy (AUP)

When it applies

Referenced in the MSA. Governs what the client can and cannot do with Corner.

What clients CAN do

  • Use Corner for legitimate business operations
  • Configure agents and skills for their specific workflows
  • Access their data at any time
  • Export their data at any time
  • Share their dashboard access with authorized team members (when multi-user launches in C7)

What clients CANNOT do

  • Use Corner to generate spam, phishing content, or deceptive communications
  • Use Corner for illegal activities (fraud, harassment, discrimination)
  • Attempt to access other clients' data or systems
  • Reverse-engineer, decompile, or replicate Corner's architecture
  • Use Corner to generate content that violates third-party intellectual property
  • Share login credentials with unauthorized parties
  • Use Corner to store or process regulated data (HIPAA, PCI) without AOM's explicit written agreement and appropriate compliance measures
  • Exceed reasonable usage limits (defined per tier) through automated abuse or data flooding
  • Resell or sublicense access to Corner without AOM's written agreement

Enforcement

  • First violation: written warning with 7 days to cure
  • Second violation: 30-day suspension
  • Third violation or severe first violation (illegal activity, data breach attempt): immediate termination

Implementation Checklist

  1. Patrik: Get cyber insurance quote. The policy dictates what the agreements can and can't promise. This is step zero.
  2. Patrik: Find a business attorney. Phoenix-based, tech-savvy, familiar with SaaS agreements. Budget: $2,000-$4,000 for all three documents drafted and reviewed.
  3. Steve: Deliver this spec to the attorney. This document IS the brief. The attorney turns it into legally enforceable language.
  4. Patrik: Review and sign off on drafts.
  5. Bobby: Build a DocuSign or equivalent e-signature flow so clients can sign digitally during onboarding.
  6. Steffen: Design a branded cover page for the NDA and MSA PDFs. Clean, professional, AOM brand.

Attorney Selection Criteria

  • Experience with SaaS/technology agreements
  • Familiar with AI liability landscape (this is evolving fast)
  • Understands small business clients (not overly complex language)
  • Phoenix-based (Arizona law governs)
  • Budget-friendly. AOM doesn't need a BigLaw firm for these documents.

Budget Estimate

  • Attorney drafting + review: $2,000-$4,000
  • E-signature platform: $0-$25/month (DocuSign Essentials or free alternatives)
  • Cyber insurance: varies (Patrik getting quote)
  • Total setup: ~$2,500-$4,500 one-time

What This Spec Does NOT Cover

  • SOC 2 compliance specifics. That's a separate initiative (Elon's domain). The MSA references AOM's security practices but doesn't claim SOC 2 certification until AOM has it.
  • HIPAA/PCI compliance. If AOM takes healthcare or payment processing clients, those require additional agreements. Not in scope for C3/C4.
  • International terms. When Corner goes international (C9), each market needs localized legal terms. Not relevant today.
  • Franchise agreements. C8 territory. Separate legal workstream.

The first client needs three signatures: NDA, MSA, AUP. That's it. Three documents that protect AOM, protect the client, and set clear expectations. This spec gives the attorney everything they need to draft all three. The only blocker is the cyber insurance quote. That's a phone call.
